title: Hidden authentication tokens can traverse the WebView settings patch request

locations.symbol: Keys not offered in WebView raw JSON

observed_behavior: The backend accepts a real value for a registered sensitive key through the ordinary settings patch candidate path; it rejects only the literal <redacted> placeholder and redacts response evidence after the secret has already entered the browser request path.
expected_invariant: CoordinatorAuthToken and WorkerAuthToken must not enter browser storage, DevTools-visible request bodies, or JavaScript heap state, as the active architecture guidance requires.
root_cause: The patch allowlist has no request-side exclusion or purpose-built secret channel for sensitive keys; sensitive-key handling is limited to placeholder rejection and response redaction.
failure_scenario: An operator or authenticated local page caller pastes a replacement coordinator token into raw Settings JSON. The token enters JavaScript state and the HTTP request and is accepted for preview/save even though rendered review evidence is redacted.
evidence: Current candidate source at lines 295-318 is unchanged from the independently reproduced July 19 baseline.
The focused current test passed while submitting CoordinatorAuthToken=new-secret-token and asserting a successful redacted preview.
SETTINGS_RAW_KEY_TRIAGE.md lines 72-77 explicitly prohibit these tokens from browser storage, DevTools, and JS heap snapshots.
Prior validation record VAL-0016 independently confirmed the same production path.
affected_flows: WebView Settings raw patch -> Local API preview/save -> backend candidate validation
network coordinator/worker authentication-secret lifecycle
existing_safeguards: Loopback authentication, strict save confirmation, redacted placeholder rejection, recursive response redaction, and review-confirmation binding reduce unauthorized writes and response leakage.
safeguard_gap: None of those controls prevents the real secret from being created and transported inside the browser process and request payload.
tests_missing: Negative facade and HTTP tests rejecting real sensitive-key patch values
WebView boundary test proving token values never enter settings request/client state
Purpose-built native secret-rotation channel tests if such a channel is introduced
recommended_remediation: Reject sensitive config keys on ordinary preview/save patch routes and expose any required rotation through a separately designed backend/native credential flow that never stages the secret in WebView state.
remediation_risk: medium-high: changes an existing accepted settings path and must preserve secure rotation and existing secrets without browser disclosure
validation_rung: Targeted settings facade/Local API/security tests, WebView mutation-boundary checks, packaged Windows secret-rotation proof, and strict change-packet coverage; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Confirmed carry-forward of CSW-2026-07-09-SETTINGS-001; affected production and architecture files are unchanged and current focused evidence still reproduces acceptance.

category: configuration authority and runtime namespace integrity
title: Legacy extras remain executable runtime configuration
observed_behavior: Every preserved legacy extra is merged into the active PSD1 projection, and every non-reserved imported key is assigned into PowerShell script scope. Active docs describe the same extras as inert and non-policy authority.
expected_invariant: Unknown compatibility data may round-trip for recovery, but it must not silently become an executable runtime variable or influence media policy unless it is registered and validated by the shared config schema.
root_cause: Compatibility preservation, projection generation, schema validation, and runtime variable materialization do not share one allowlist boundary; projection and runtime merge treat unknown keys as active values.
failure_scenario: A retired, misspelled, or laboratory-only PSD1 key is imported as a legacy extra. It is projected back to PSD1 and materialized in script scope; a current or future engine module with the same variable name then consumes unregistered policy without schema validation.
evidence: _projection_values updates canonical settings with the complete legacy_extras mapping.
runtime_merge.ps1 calls Set-Variable -Scope Script for every key except a finite reserved-name denylist.
A current no-write bundled-PowerShell probe returned Exists=true and Value=keep-for-projection for LegacyLabOnlyToggle.
API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md and MODULE_MAP.md explicitly call legacy extras inert, contradicting executable truth.
The materializing source paths are unchanged from the independently verified July 19 reproduction.
affected_flows: PSD1 import -> JSON authority legacy_extras -> PSD1 projection -> PowerShell runtime merge
configuration schema/default/persistence/runtime-consumption authority
existing_safeguards: Known settings are Pydantic/schema validated, canonical spelling is enforced, and a reserved PowerShell variable denylist blocks preference and automatic-variable collisions.
safeguard_gap: Unknown non-reserved names bypass known-key validation and are still promoted into the live script namespace; the denylist cannot anticipate future policy variable names.
tests_missing: Execution-level negative test proving unknown extras never enter active PSD1 or script scope
Schema test rejecting unregistered runtime keys while retaining archival round-trip data
Compatibility migration test for retired/misspelled keys
recommended_remediation: Keep legacy extras only in archival JSON/projection-manifest evidence, exclude them from the active PSD1, and make runtime merge accept only the canonical shared key registry; alternatively reject unknown PSD1 keys before runtime initialization.
remediation_risk: medium-high: compatibility and recovery semantics change and must not discard operator evidence or silently alter registered media policy
validation_rung: Settings-store/import/schema tests, actual PowerShell runtime-merge tests, packaged config reload/restart proof, representative policy sampling, and strict change-packet coverage; no source media mutation is needed.
prior_audit_relationship: Confirmed carry-forward of CSW-2026-07-09-SETTINGS-002; prior inert closure is disproven by unchanged code and a fresh current-tree no-write reproduction.

category: generated navigation and audit coverage integrity
title: Generated summaries and project index do not describe the current worktree
observed_behavior: Canonical check modes found 10 missing and 37 stale summaries; project-index generation expected 2,425 records versus 2,410 checked in; 66 indexed source hashes were stale; six summarized sources were absent from the index and one indexed source lacked a summary.
expected_invariant: Generated navigation must be reproducible from current source, have check-mode agreement, and reconcile every represented source, summary, hash, and dependency edge before it is used as audit or agent-navigation evidence.
root_cause: Source and documentation changes accumulated without the canonical summary and project-index generators being refreshed as one stable phase-boundary transaction; concurrent worktree edits then widened the snapshot drift.
failure_scenario: An audit worker follows a stale summary, owner, associated-test list, or dependency edge and incorrectly omits a changed file or trusts behavior that no longer matches source, producing false coverage or a misplaced remediation.
evidence: refresh_summaries --check exited 1 with 10 missing and 37 stale summaries (AUDIT-ERR-COVERAGE-002).
generate_project_index --check exited 1 and expected 2,425 records rather than 2,410 (AUDIT-ERR-COVERAGE-003).
Deterministic hash comparison found 66 stale source_hash values among 2,410 index rows (AUDIT-ERR-COVERAGE-010).
Summary/index set reconciliation found six summary-only sources and one index-only source (AUDIT-ERR-COVERAGE-013).
affected_flows: AGENTS.md context-slice and generated-summary navigation
file ownership, dependency, risk, and associated-test assignment
audit coverage universe reconciliation
existing_safeguards: Both generators expose deterministic check modes, summary frontmatter carries source hashes, and generated-integrity tests can detect drift.
safeguard_gap: The checked-in/current-worktree artifacts are presently red, and ordinary concurrent edits are not transactionally frozen before audit consumers read them.

title: Effective-config dump omits registered runtime safety and autonomy settings
observed_behavior: The dump helper claims to enumerate every config-derived runtime variable but its manual list omits 17 registered values assigned by runtime initialization, including pending-publish backlog/drain controls, pause and failure thresholds, local-worker heartbeat grace, queue round/freshness caps, SQLite maintenance limits, subtitle-helper fallback, interrupted-log retention, and debug-log size.
expected_invariant: The operator-facing effective-config dump must accurately expose every behavior-defining runtime setting it claims to cover, especially values that block queue work, authorize trusted drain posture, control recovery, or bound retained evidence.
root_cause: Runtime initialization and effective-dump membership are separately hand-maintained; no executable parity assertion ties registered script-scope config assignments to the diagnostic name list.
failure_scenario: A queue becomes blocked by PendingPublishBacklogBlockThreshold or ConsecutiveRoundFailureBlockLimit, or a trusted drain/debug retention setting differs from the operator's expectation. DumpEffectiveConfigPath succeeds but omits the controlling value, so diagnostics falsely appear complete and triage assumes an unrelated default or policy.
evidence: Static set comparison of script-scope assignments in runtime_config.ps1 against quoted dump names produced 17 registered assigned-but-undumped values after excluding internal ActiveOverrides, CurrentSizePolicyResult, and LastQualityVerification.
Each omitted name is present in config_keys.ps1 and config_key_groups.py; active CONFIG_KEY_GLOSSARY rows document their behavior and risk.
runtime_paths.ps1 lines 11-14 explicitly describe the list as every config-derived runtime variable.
Repository search found no direct test reference to Get-MediaPipelineResolvedConfigDump; ConfigKeyRegistryChecks passed 206 registered keys while leaving dump parity unchecked.
affected_flows: PowerShell runtime config initialization -> DumpEffectiveConfigPath diagnostic artifact
queue/autonomy/pending-publish/recovery/storage observability
operator incident triage and reproducibility evidence
existing_safeguards: Values are individually registered, range-normalized, documented, and scanned by the 206-key ConfigKeyRegistryChecks suite; the dump is sorted and stable for names it includes.
safeguard_gap: Registry/reference checks do not verify diagnostic membership, so new behavior settings can be fully valid yet invisible from the supposedly complete effective dump.
tests_present: Current no-write ConfigKeyRegistryChecks run passed with 206 keys and 166 PowerShell files scanned
tests_missing: Exact parity test between behavior-defining runtime config assignments and effective-dump names
Disposable DumpEffectiveConfigPath execution asserting the 17 omitted settings and normalized values
Regression proving new config keys cannot land without an explicit dump inclusion/exclusion disposition
recommended_remediation: Derive the effective dump from a shared registry annotated for runtime diagnostics, or add an exact maintained parity contract that requires every runtime setting to be included or explicitly excluded with rationale; add the currently omitted values.
remediation_risk: low-medium: diagnostic-only shape expansion, but consumers and snapshots may depend on stable keys and sensitive values must remain explicitly excluded
validation_rung: PowerShell config-registry/unit checks, disposable effective-dump execution, schema/docs parity, release diagnostics smoke, and strict change-packet coverage; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New root cause discovered during current worker-02 line review; related to but distinct from the July 19 stale settings-inventory count finding.

category: architecture dependency boundary and validation gate
title: Process preflight imports queue policy and reopens the core package cycle
observed_behavior: The current process preflight facade imports six queue.freshness symbols. Canonical dependency analysis finds no module-level cycle, but those imports add mediapipeline.core.processes -> mediapipeline.core.queue to a 13-package strongly connected component and leave the edge as the sole unallowlisted hard finding, so the default dependency-boundary gate exits 1.
expected_invariant: Core domain packages must preserve the enforced directionality contract, and the canonical dependency-boundary gate must have zero unallowlisted hard findings. Cross-domain freshness policy needed by process preflight must live in a lower-level shared authority or be consumed through an allowed owner boundary without adding a package cycle.
root_cause: Queue snapshot freshness policy and constants are owned by the queue package even though process launch preflight also consumes them; preflight directly crosses into that higher-level domain instead of depending on a lower-level contract/policy owner.
failure_scenario: Any release, guardrail, or developer check that runs dependency boundaries fails on an otherwise valid change. More importantly, queue and process policy can now evolve through a cyclic package graph, increasing import-order and ownership ambiguity on launch-readiness behavior.
evidence: Canonical default command exited 1 with 3,943 imports, zero module cycles, one package cycle, 39 hard findings, 38 allowlisted findings, and exactly one unallowlisted NO_PACKAGE_CYCLES edge (AUDIT-ERR-COORD-023).
Compact --format json --report-only extraction identified six imports at preflight_facade.py line 17, all from mediapipeline.core.queue.freshness, and no parse or allowlist errors.

The source content SHA-256 2d37bca0fedf83cb8b5d840911e745e3a175e3848e9bf99ab4a2be68bb486240 matches its generated summary; Git blob 503f3fe1c16f028f4a08d2656c1b1a0e7525a227 is clean in the current worktree.
MP-CHANGE-2026-0720-024 independently records the same pre-existing gate blocker through preflight_facade.py, but no current or prior audit finding register assigned it a disposition.
affected_flows: pipeline/audit/rerun launch preflight and queue snapshot freshness evaluation
AI guardrail and dependency-boundary validation
core package ownership and import directionality
existing_safeguards: check_dependency_boundaries deterministically computes module and package SCCs
hard rules use an explicit allowlist and default fail-closed exit behavior
tests/python/tooling/test_dependency_boundaries.py exercises the analyzer and enforcement surface
safeguard_gap: The safeguard correctly detects the new edge, but the checked-in architecture still violates it and no allowlist rationale or refactoring resolves the ownership crossing.
tests_missing: A focused ownership test proving queue freshness primitives reside below both queue and process preflight
A regression fixture asserting the production graph has no unallowlisted processes-to-queue package edge
recommended_remediation: Move queue snapshot freshness constants/evaluation into a lower-level contracts or policy module legitimately shared by queue and process launch preflight, then update both consumers and remove the processes-to-queue edge. Do not merely allowlist the edge without a time-bounded architectural rationale.
remediation_risk: medium: queue snapshot freshness affects launch admission and stale-plan safety, so relocation must preserve constants, normalization, clock-skew handling, result schema, and all queue/preflight callers
validation_rung: Targeted queue freshness and launch-preflight tests, dependency-boundary unit tests, canonical dependency gate, AI guardrail postflight, generated dependency/context checks, and strict change-packet coverage; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit finding; a concurrent July 20 change packet called the edge pre-existing and unrelated but did not provide an audit disposition. The June finding register has no equivalent root cause.

title: Metrics reports sidecar discovery complete before every enabled source has a successful full scan
observed_behavior: A newly configured enabled source with no backfill status is reported with last_backfill_status=not_run and completeness.complete=true. With two enabled sources, scanning only one by source_id produces root statuses complete and never but still reports global sidecar discovery and Metrics completeness as true.
expected_invariant: Sidecar-discovery completeness may be true only when every enabled source has current evidence of a successful full scan, or when no enabled sources require discovery; a targeted scan must not certify untouched roots.
root_cause: _source_state_from_registry derives discovery completeness from cache parse health plus one aggregate last-status file. The not_run state is not treated as incomplete, and the aggregate status records only the most recent requested scan scope instead of reconciling every enabled root's last_scan_status.
failure_scenario: An operator adds multiple legacy-library roots, runs a targeted backfill for one, and sees global Metrics completeness marked complete even though other enabled roots were never searched. Missing historical sidecars can then be mistaken for an actually complete inventory.
evidence: Isolated temporary-state probe after adding one enabled source returned add_ok=true, last_backfill_status=not_run, complete=true, source_count=1, cache_count=0.

A second isolated probe added two enabled roots and scanned only source A; the backfill status was complete, the roots reported A=complete and B=never, enabled cache count was one, and global completeness remained true.
Source lines 283-288 exclude partial, warning, blocked, and unreachable but not not_run, while lines 303-308 publish the resulting boolean.
Facade lines 57-75 directly elevate that source boolean into sidecar_discovery_complete and global Metrics completeness.
The focused Metrics/backfill suites passed 17 tests and the degraded browser smoke passed, confirming the never-scanned/mixed-root invariant is presently untested rather than already enforced.
affected_flows: Metrics source registry and recursive sidecar backfill
Local API /api/metrics completeness
operator interpretation of legacy sidecar discovery coverage
existing_safeguards: Each root retains last_scan_status, partial/warning scans preserve the prior complete cache, cache parsing exposes health, and Metrics emits a separate warning when enabled roots have no cached rows.
safeguard_gap: No safeguard reconciles all enabled-root scan states into the global completeness flag, so a warning or per-root never marker can coexist with a false-green top-level status.
tests_missing: A newly added enabled source must keep discovery completeness false until its first full scan succeeds
A targeted scan of one of multiple enabled sources must not mark global discovery complete
Disabling the only never-scanned root should recompute completeness from the remaining enabled roots
recommended_remediation: Compute discovery completeness from every enabled registry entry: require last_scan_status=complete for each enabled root (and healthy cache/status evidence), while defining the zero-enabled-source case explicitly. Add focused state and Local API regression tests for never-scanned and mixed targeted-scan cases.
remediation_risk: low-medium: diagnostic state only, but downstream UI and automation may rely on the current completeness boolean and status transitions
validation_rung: Focused Metrics source/facade unit tests, Local API contract tests, browser degraded-state smoke, generated-context refresh, and strict change-packet coverage; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash operational finding; prior frozen review bytes and existing tests did not cover the never-scanned or mixed-root completeness cases.

title: Folder-policy max_files caps probes only after an unbounded full-tree enumeration and sort
observed_behavior: validate_folder_policy accepts max_files (default 8) but first recursively enumerates every descendant, resolves every matching media path, materializes the complete list, and sorts it. Only afterward does it slice the probe list. An isolated max_files=1 probe with seven candidates enumerated all seven while probing one.
expected_invariant: A caller-visible file bound on an operator validation workflow should bound expensive recursive discovery as well as ffprobe executions, or the API must expose and enforce a separate discovery/time budget with explicit partial evidence.
root_cause: The implementation constructs a globally sorted media_files list with folder.rglob before applying max_files to selected, so deterministic ordering requires full traversal and retains every candidate path in memory.
failure_scenario: Validating a very large show/library tree from a synchronous desktop workflow can spend minutes walking and sorting hundreds of thousands of paths despite max_files=8, delaying the response and consuming memory before the first bounded probe completes.
evidence: Source lines 98-101 materialize and sort the full rglob result; lines 115-116 apply max_files only afterward.
An isolated temporary-folder probe patched rglob to count yields: max_files=1 enumerated=7, probed=1, checked_count=1, ok=true.
All 22 focused file-open/folder-policy tests pass; none asserts a discovery bound, scan cap, partial result, or time budget.
Repository search found no active Local API caller, reducing immediate exposure but leaving the backend service contract unbounded if invoked by an approved workflow.
affected_flows: folder-policy validation and sample selection
desktop/service responsiveness on large recursive roots
operator confidence in max_files as a work bound
existing_safeguards: ffprobe calls are individually timeout-bounded, max_files limits the number of probes, validation is dry-run unless save=true, and samples are constrained inside the folder.
safeguard_gap: No candidate-count, traversal-time, directory-count, cancellation, or partial-discovery bound applies before probing.
tests_missing: A traversal-count/time budget regression proving max_files does not require full-tree materialization
A partial-discovery status contract for capped scans
A large-tree responsiveness test or explicit documented separate discovery bound
recommended_remediation: Use a bounded deterministic iterator or introduce explicit max_candidates/time/cancellation controls and return partial-discovery evidence. Preserve sample precedence and folder containment, and document that probe and discovery bounds are distinct if both remain configurable.
remediation_risk: low-medium: changing discovery order or cap semantics can change which files form the validation sample, so deterministic ordering and saved expected_topology must remain stable
validation_rung: Focused folder-policy contract/IO/probe tests, new bounded-discovery tests, an isolated large-tree timing/cap probe, and strict change-packet coverage; representative real media is not required for the bound itself.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash operational finding; earlier ownership reviews noted the service but did not measure the pre-probe traversal bound.
